content: A disabled millennial columnist describes feeling fortunate merely to leave the house and warns that everyday social activities — going to work, meeting friends, seeing people — are no longer guaranteed; new research from Scope finds nearly half of working-age disabled people in Britain “always or often” feel lonely (about 3 million people), a finding that adds to the Office for National Statistics’ characterization of Britain as Europe’s “loneliness capital” and suggests a severe epidemic of isolation among disabled people.
